_notes: Compiled by Tom Collins, based on st_162h by HorsePin
player_count added at 0x02110900, the one address shared across every Stern SAM game checked --
24, X-Men, LUCI and both Star Trek revisions, over ten captures at one, two and four players.
The declared score slots were confirmed on hardware rather than assumed: a 4-player game ending
1,236,620 / 2,197,850 / 1,137,910 / 1,714,440 read back exactly at 0x02110A0C on a 4-byte stride.
current_player and current_ball are still unmapped. Neither is retained in NVRAM after a game,
and a sweep of 0x0-0x3FFFF did not produce the adjacent pair that identified them on X-Men and
LUCI, so they are somewhere else in CPU RAM.
current_player/current_ball came from the joint pair test -- the player wrapping to 1 in the same
sample the ball steps up -- which returned exactly one hit across a full four-player game.
Unlike trn_174h and twd_156c, this ROM resets both counters to 1 at game end, so its exit dump
reads 1/1 rather than the 4/3 that confirmed those two. The single in-play hit is the evidence
here; the dump neither confirms nor contradicts it.
Scores verified against the same dump: 2,032,370 / 1,248,620 / 1,330,340 / 1,342,740 at 4-byte
centres from 0x02110A0C, where stride 8 runs into the 0xFFFFFFFF fill. The sweep independently
reproduced this map's existing score address, and rejected a CPU RAM candidate at 0x00038D9C
whose four values (~16.7M, near-identical) are the usual scaled-set false positive.
Free Play is one entry in the machine adjustments array, which begins at 0x02102008 and runs
as 8-byte records: a 32-bit little-endian value followed by a 4-byte field whose low byte is
0xFF minus the sum of the value's four bytes, padded with 0xFF above. Every record in the
array satisfies that, so writing an adjustment without updating its check byte leaves the
game discarding the change on the next load.
The address was measured by toggling Free Play in the operator menu and diffing NVRAM either
side: the value goes 1 -> 0 and the check byte 0xFE -> 0xFF, equal and opposite.
The check byte is expressed as a checksum8 record because checksum8 is defined as
complement-to-0xFF, which is exactly this rule; it is adjacent to the value, so no separate
checksum address is needed.
Note the operator menu calls this Standard Adjustment #38 on all three games measured, but it
is not the 38th record of this array -- it lands at index 33 here and 35 on st_162h. The menu
numbering does not index the array directly, so the address is measured per game, not derived.
